transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording id: ff-20260520-0742-lakemont

Summary: quick renewal checkin, customer exploring a retainer uplift (stretch) and EU onprem/VPC pathway for PHI-sensitive flows. Discussed cost/latency tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Private, SLA amendments, and next steps to run a small benchmark and draft SOW.

Topics: retainer uplift, EU VPC onramp, KMS + encryption, SSO/SAML, staging benchmarks, rollout timeline

Questions: are we hitting latency SLOs today? what does EU onprem pilot look like? pricing uplift amortization?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya Shah: ok hey everyone im Priya from Redwood, thanks for making time, how's it going in boston?
[00:06] Dr. Aisha Rahman: good thanks, bit of a busy week but excited to get this aligned, we've got Tom and Lena on for ops and security.
[00:11] Tom Avery: yeah hi all, we'll be brief — main thing is we need clarity on the retainer numbers and the eu vpc approach.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: sounds good; i'll focus on the technical bits, network, benchmarks etc. quick call outline: talk current usage, proposed uplift, EU private/vpc options, security needs, and define next steps.
[00:32] [crosstalk] Marco Diaz: quick clarification, when you say EU onprem do you mean fully on-prem or VPC-private in eu-cloud?
[00:38] Priya Shah: great question — we typically offer two paths: Redwood Private (customer VPC or on-prem pack) or dedicated with EU-hosted nodes; for PHI we usually recommend Private VPC so keys and network are customer-managed.
[00:51] Dr. Aisha Rahman: ok, so we want customer-managed network + k m s for key custody; our legal requires data residency in eu and audit logs retained 7 years — is that supported?
[01:03] Jules Park: yes we have audit log retention options and enterprise packages that cover extended retention, SOC2 plus ISO 27001 support — we'll share the compliance pack after.
[01:11] Lena Ortiz: also need SSO with SAML and RBAC enforced for dev/test/prod — and separation of dev keys.
[01:18] Marcus Lee: technically that's fine; we can integrate with your IdP, set up RBAC via our console, and provision KMS/HSM integrations in the private control plane. small note: on-prem path adds lead time for onprem appliance but VPC peering is usually faster.
[01:33] Tom Avery: timeline is important — we want a pilot in EU for October but need the contract in place by end of June to align budgets.
[01:41] Priya Shah: understood. on the retainer, you currently have ~7M tokens/month on the hosted plan? can you confirm baseline and spikes?
[01:50] Dr. Aisha Rahman: baseline is 6.8M tokens, spikes up to 12M during seasonal peak. our finance team wants predictability — so looking at a 20-25% uplift in committed capacity.
[02:03] Priya Shah: ok that's helpful. our proposal would be a retainer stretch to cover the spikes — typically a blended price where dedicated capacity reduces unit cost. we'll draft numbers.
[02:13] Marcus Lee: on perf, important to know latency SLOs — what's acceptable? median vs p95?
[02:18] Tom Avery: p95 under 250ms is our goal for user-facing chat flows; batch embed jobs can be higher.
[02:24] Marcus Lee: that's achievable with a eu-dedicated pool and optimized batching; if you go full onprem there's more tuning but fallback routing is available.
[02:33] [30s silence while screen shared]
[03:02] Marco Diaz: question: what about kv cache and prefix caching? we rely heavily on cached prompts — will that transfer to private deployment?
[03:10] Marcus Lee: yes KV cache semantics preserve; when we provision private we replicate the runtime with same caching; small name mismatch sometimes in logs but functionally identical.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: any encryption in transit and at rest specifics we should call out? especially for patient data.
[03:26] Jules Park: in private mode you can bring your own KMS; traffic between your VPC and our control plane can be peered with encryption and IP allowlists. we'll attach the security whitepaper.
[03:38] Dr. Aisha Rahman: on pricing, how do we amortize the uplift? is it monthly charge + reserved GPU commit?
[03:45] Priya Shah: typically a retainer is monthly committed tokens plus a reserved capacity fee for dedicated pools; the math depends on the commitment term — longer term reduces unit price. we'll model 12 vs 24 month.
[03:56] Tom Avery: we prefer a 12 month extension with a runway to evaluate onprem. can you do a clause for pilot to convert to onprem if benchmarks pass?
[04:05] Priya Shah: yes we can add a pilot-to-convert clause; legal will draft options — it's a common pattern.
[04:12] Marcus Lee: for the benchmark, we'd like Lakemont to provide 3 representative prompt sets (chat, triage, embeddings) and we'll run a 2-hour baseline with p95, p99, and token cost.
[04:23] Marco Diaz: we can do that, we'll annotate prompts with expected sequence lengths.
[04:27] Lena Ortiz: security wants to validate key lifecycle and HSM integration in the pilot — can Redwood provide test vectors?
[04:35] Marcus Lee: yes we'll provide a test harness and runbook; it includes KMS rotate tests and sample audit events.
[04:42] [conversation — pricing back-and-forth, numbers slightly garbled by transcript]
[05:05] Priya Shah: rough numbers as of now: stretch to 8.5M committed tokens with a 12 month extension; reserved compute fee to be scoped after benchmark; rough uplift of 18-22% on current monthly bill. we'll formalize in the SOW.
[05:21] Dr. Aisha Rahman: that seems in line. finance will need a clear amortization schedule, can you include that in the SOW?
[05:28] Priya Shah: yes we'll include month-by-month cost and unit price assumptions.
[05:33] Tom Avery: on network, we'll need a VPC peering and a small NAT/proxy for logs export; Marco will coordinate.
[05:42] Marco Diaz: i'll send CIDR ranges and firewall rules tonight.
[05:46] Marcus Lee: also note that EU onprem provisioning has a 6-8 week lead for physical appliance; VPC peering in cloud is about 2-3 weeks.
[05:55] Lena Ortiz: can you confirm data purge options in Private? retention windows etc.
[06:00] Jules Park: yes, Private gives control over retention; we can configure auto-purge after X days and preserve audit logs per retention policy.
[06:07] Dr. Aisha Rahman: final question — do you support SOC2 log pulls for audits?
[06:11] Jules Park: yes we'll provide exportable audit logs and a supporting compliance pack.
[06:16] [wrap up] Priya Shah: recap: Priya will send SOW draft with retainer stretch numbers and pilot clause; Marcus sends EU VPC runbook and bench plan; Marco shares network info; Lena shares KMS policy. schedule benchmark week of 2026-06-01.
[06:33] Tom Avery: sounds great, thanks everyone.
[06:37] Dr. Aisha Rahman: thanks, look forward to the SOW.
[06:40] Priya Shah: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and Slack.
[06:44] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcript quality: stutters and minor transcription errors around numeric values and product names (e.g., "redwood dedicate" in place of "Redwood Dedicated"). Some speaker alignment may be off when multiple people speak.

Shared artifacts referenced: SOW template (link sent in chat), Redwood EU VPC runbook (to be shared), Security/compliance pack (SOC2/ISO papers).

End of transcript.
